key_insight: DCSD separates step-level credit direction from credit magnitude so self-distillation can calibrate teacher supervision with more reliable signals.
engineering_relevance: The method is relevant for training reasoning models because it improves credit assignment during policy optimization, especially when teacher feedback is noisy or preference-variant.
method: Belief-margin probing estimates the direction of credit assignment.
Marginal information gain quantifies the magnitude of each step’s contribution.
These signals are used to decouple step-to-token credit and calibrate privileged teacher supervision.
evidence_signal: Across 11 benchmarks, DCSD reports the best overall scores versus GRPO, OPSD, RLSD, and RLCSD, with +8.45 points on mathematical reasoning and +7.01 on multimodal reasoning.
watch_item: The approach depends on additional probing and information-gain estimation, so its robustness and compute cost may vary across models and tasks.
paper_title: Can We Trust the Teacher? Decoupled Credit Direction-Magnitude for Self-Distillation
